Are you curious about digital marketing and ready to take your next step in paid advertising, helping grow a subscription business across Europe?

Goodiebox has transformed significantly over the past three years. We have delivered consistent positive EBITDA, become an AI-first company, and are now combining month-on-month growth with continued profitability across 15 European markets.

We’re looking for a structured and curious Junior Paid Social Specialist to support our Growth Lead across Meta, TikTok, Google and YouTube. You’ll work with campaigns, creatives and performance data, learning how paid advertising contributes to profitable growth.

You’ll join a seven-person Growth Team, working alongside passionate colleagues with an approximately DKK 2 million monthly growth budget. Together, we work to attract more members, improve acquisition costs and conversion across the full funnel, and strengthen the long-term value of the members we acquire.

This is an opportunity to build on your knowledge, learn from experienced colleagues and gradually take on more responsibility as you develop your skills.

Your role

You’ll report directly to our Growth Lead and become part of our Growth Team, working alongside colleagues across Creative, Social Media, Retention and Development.

Your main focus will be supporting the day-to-day execution of our advertising activities. That means making sure campaigns launch correctly, keeping our work organized and helping us understand what drives performance.

You don’t need to arrive as an expert. Some hands-on experience with paid social is a big plus, whether from a previous role, an internship or your own projects. Above all, we’re looking for someone who enjoys working with numbers, pays attention to detail and is eager to learn.

What you’ll do

• 
Build and launch campaigns: Support campaign setup across Meta, TikTok, Google and YouTube, including uploading creatives, creating compelling ad copy, testing new landing pages and ensuring every launch is smooth.

• 
Monitor performance: Help track spend and results across markets, spot changes and flag opportunities or issues to the Growth Lead.

• 
Support reporting and analysis: Maintain performance reports and turn data into clear observations that help guide our next steps.

• 
Help improve our creatives: Work with the Growth Lead and our in-house creators to identify promising ads, prepare creative variations and share learnings from performance.

• 
Keep testing organized: Support creative and campaign experiments, track what we’re testing and document results so we can build on what we learn.

• 
Maintain structure and quality: Keep naming conventions, campaign assets and tracking links consistent, and support coordination across markets.

• 
Use AI in your daily work: Explore tools that help with analysis, copy variations and repetitive tasks, while checking the quality and accuracy of the output.

Who we’re looking for

You’re likely studying marketing, business, communications or a related field. Most importantly, you’re interested in digital marketing and motivated to put that interest into practice.

We imagine that you:

• 
Have a structured approach and enjoy keeping track of details, tasks and deadlines.

• 
Are comfortable working with numbers and curious about why performance changes.

• 
Have a basic working knowledge of Excel or Google Sheets.

• 
Take initiative, follow through and ask questions when something is unclear.

• 
Have a commercial mindset and want to understand how advertising contributes to business results.

• 
Communicate clearly in English; a Nordic language is a plus.

• 
Are curious about AI and open to learning new tools.

Ideally, you’ve already had some exposure to advertising platforms, campaign setup or performance reporting. Experience is a plus, but not a requirement if you bring a structured approach, curiosity and a strong motivation to learn.

What we offer

• 
Structured onboarding and hands-on training in advertising platforms.

• 
Close mentorship and regular feedback from our Growth Lead.

• 
Experience working with live campaigns across multiple European markets.

• 
Collaboration with in-house creatives and other marketing specialists.

• 
Growing responsibility as you develop your skills.

• 
A collaborative environment where your ideas and observations are welcome.

Practical information

Hours: Approximately 16-24 hours per week, with the schedule agreed around your studies.

Location: Islands Brygge, Copenhagen. Primarily based in our office.

Start date: 1st of December.

Application deadline: We interview on an ongoing basis, so send us your application as soon as possible.

Please include your CV, a few lines about why you’re interested and your weekly availability.

Job organizational context:

The Global Transport & Logistics Center (GTLC) within the UNICEF Supply Division in Copenhagen is accountable for securing adequate service provision to deliver development and emergency supplies from vendors or UNICEF hubs to all UNICEF COs and Partners and for the ability to go beyond the port of entry up to the last mile.

This is possible through establishing a five-year intermodal transport contract with global freight forwarders and MOUs with leading carriers. This strategy also aims to support and streamline processes and systems for efficient and timely international transport services and, delivery solutions for UNICEF COs and Partners to secure an end-to-end sustainable supply chain for all countries where UNICEF is present.

In line with the systems strengthening strategy, UNICEF is collaborating with the Global and address bottlenecks in the importation of critical supplies for children, such as vaccines, auxiliary supplies and cold chain equipment; medicines and medical devices; sanitation equipment; and implement appropriate country level process improvement initiatives.

How can you make a difference?

Under the supervision of the GTLC Logistics Manager, the Project Manager will support the ongoing implementation of the ADEPT Programme in existing and additional countries by improving and building systems that enable faster importation, including fiscal and regulatory processes, and clearance of health products, vaccines, and other commodities. The role will also support global policy engagement, importation process improvement initiatives, and stronger public-private collaboration at global and country levels to ensure the timely, efficient, and cost-effective delivery of essential goods to children and vulnerable communities.

• The Project Manager will engage UNICEF offices in mutually agreed countries to support in-country project delivery, as required, by:

• Validating and establishing in-country information and relevant contacts during the initial project validation phase.

• Liaising with relevant stakeholders, including ministries of health and other government agencies, to obtain and maintain support for project activities and working-level collaboration.

• Supporting diagnostic work to map importation processes, including tax exemptions, regulatory approvals, and other clearance requirements.

• Establishing and sourcing the data needed to measure baseline performance and project impact, including time and cost indicators.

• Participating in project governance structures, workshops, and convenings based on diagnostic missions and agreed implementation needs.

• When on mission the Project Manager will collaborate with GATF counterparts on below work assignment overview:

• Convene workshops/joint activities to coordinate the streamlining of the country’s importation processes and procedures and advocate for a single window.

• Enhancing the understanding of each country specificity on importation processes and Customs Clearance requirements to reduce NTBs (non-tariffs barriers) through evidence creation and awareness raising activities.

• Clarify with government the mechanism of financial disbursement between governments agencies and how it affects the importation processes and timelines.

• Establish, in collaboration with the Alliance, the in-country working group overseeing the project implementation as required and participate as needed in public-private working groups in-country to ensure project sustainability.

• Raise awareness of key stakeholders (Government, Humanitarian and Private Sector) on the benefit of GATF’s initiative in digitalization of the importation processes.

• Strengthening related partnerships

• Identify key stakeholders that could be strong partners to lobby or collaborate on related activities.

Do you have experience configuring, testing and commissioning control systems for high-voltage substations? Would you like to apply your expertise to projects supporting Denmark’s electricity transmission grid? Join COWI as a Substation Control and Automation Specialist.

Develop and commission substation control systems

We are looking for an experienced specialist to work on control and automation systems for Energinet’s 132–400 kV substations. Projects range from new substations to extensions, refurbishment and replacement of systems at existing sites.

You will design, configure, test and commission substation control systems, including remote terminal units (RTUs), bay control units (BCUs) and human–machine interfaces (HMIs). Working closely with other specialists, you will ensure that these systems operate correctly and integrate with the substation’s primary equipment, protection systems and communication infrastructure.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Design and configure substation control and monitoring functions in accordance with functional requirements and customer specifications.

• Configure, test and commission RTUs, bay control units and HMIs.

• Configure and verify communication interfaces between control devices, protection equipment and remote control systems.

• Plan and perform functional and integration testing to verify control functions, signal exchange and correct operation of system interfaces.

• Troubleshoot configuration, communication and interface issues in collaboration with other technical specialists.

• Prepare and maintain configuration documentation, test procedures and test records.

• Coordinate technical interfaces with colleagues responsible for protection, communication systems, electrical design and primary equipment

• Undertake the designated on-site role of “holdleder” when required and subject to the relevant qualifications and authorisation.

Your expertise

You take a systematic approach to configuration, testing and troubleshooting. You work independently, pay close attention to technical detail and collaborate effectively with colleagues, customers and suppliers. You understand how individual devices and interfaces contribute to the operation of the complete substation control system.

You will also bring:

• A relevant qualification in electrical engineering or an equivalent technical background, combined with at least five years of relevant experience with control systems for high-voltage substations.

• Demonstrated experience configuring and testing substation control equipment from multiple manufacturers.

• Practical experience with IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 60870-5-103 and IEC 61850 communication protocols and standards.

• A sound understanding of the interfaces between substation control systems, protection equipment and high-voltage primary equipment.

• Experience with functional testing, system integration and commissioning of substation control systems.

• Professional proficiency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

• The ability to obtain the required security clearance and meet the qualification and authorisation requirements for acting as “holdleder” at high-voltage substations.

Your place of work

Depending on project requirements, you may work from one of COWI’s offices in Denmark, at Energinet project locations or partly from home. Testing and commissioning activities will require attendance at the relevant project sites. Travel within Denmark is expected.

A place to work and so much more

Do you combine legal rigor with strong commercial judgment? Would you like to take ownership of commercial contracts and help keep Trackunit’s commercial momentum moving across EMEA and APJ?

As our Legal Counsel – Commercial Contracts, you will own the negotiation and drafting of Trackunit’s commercial contracts, particularly our Master Telematics Agreements (MTAs). You will work closely with our Commercial teams to move negotiations forward, reduce risk exposure, and support customer relationships where fast turnaround matters.

Alongside commercial contracting, you will contribute to broader legal, governance, and regulatory work. By taking full ownership of the commercial contracting process and playbook, you will help reduce deal cycles and free the General Counsel to focus on higher-level strategic matters.

Based in Denmark, you will join our Legal and Compliance department and report to the VP – General Counsel. This is an individual contributor role at IC3 level, with no people management responsibilities.

**What’s in it for you?

**You will have direct operational and tactical impact on commercial deal velocity, primarily across EMEA and APJ, while contributing to legal risk management across Trackunit’s contracting activity.

The role combines ownership of commercial negotiations with a broader range of legal work. Roughly half of your time will focus on commercial contract negotiation, ranging from routine to moderately complex matters using an established playbook. The remainder will cover general legal work across governance, regulatory, and compliance-adjacent matters, which can range from routine to more complex and ambiguous.

You will build a working understanding of Trackunit’s business, products, and customers, using that knowledge to provide advice that is commercially aware as well as legally sound.

**Your Responsibilities

**

• Own the negotiation and drafting of commercial contracts, particularly Master Telematics Agreements (MTAs), ensuring fast turnaround without unnecessary escalation.

• Act as a trusted legal partner to Commercial teams across EMEA and APJ, resolving standard redlines independently using the established contract playbook.

• Identify and mitigate risk exposure in contract terms, escalating to the General Counsel when terms fall outside standard playbook parameters and, where material, to the CFO/CEO.

• Support general legal, governance, and regulatory work, including data protection (GDPR) and other EU legislation, alongside commercial contracting.

• Build and maintain an understanding of Trackunit’s business, products, and customers to balance legal precision with commercial needs.

• Take full ownership of the commercial contracting process and playbook, contributing to reducing the General Counsel’s workload.

**Your focus this year

**Your immediate priority will be to address the EMEA and APJ negotiation bottleneck by building fluency and speed in MTA negotiations. You will help establish a clear, well-used contract playbook so that more redlines can be resolved without General Counsel involvement.

A secondary focus will be deepening your GDPR, data privacy, and EU regulatory knowledge to support both commercial contracts and general legal and governance work.

**Who are you?

**

• You bring 5+ years of experience in contract negotiation, ideally gained in-house or in a role with strong commercial exposure.

• You have working knowledge of GDPR and EU data- and software-related legislation.

• You have strong commercial instincts and can balance legal precision with deal pragmatism.

• Industry knowledge in software or construction technology is a plus, but is not a requirement.

• You use sound judgment to distinguish between redlines that fall within the established playbook and those that require escalation.

You will have delegated authority to approve and close redlines within the established contract playbook. Anything outside standard terms requires escalation to the General Counsel and, depending on materiality, potentially to the CFO/CEO. Understanding and applying that boundary is a core part of the role.

**Who will you work with?

**You will work most closely with our Commercial teams, including Sales and regional Pod Leaders. You will also collaborate regularly with Cyber Security, Quality, Supply Chain, and other internal legal and compliance colleagues.

Externally, you will negotiate directly with customer legal and procurement counterparts. Your communication will involve informing, advising, and negotiating, with negotiation being a defining part of your work.

The role has EU-wide scope, with a specific commercial negotiation focus on customer relationships across EMEA and APJ.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Positions in Experimental Nanophotonics and Quantum Optics
jobs.description:
The research group of Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen at the Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for two Postdoctoral Researcher positions in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics.

  Professor Mikkelsen’s group studies how light and matter interact when light is confined to nanometre-scale volumes. Using plasmonic nanocavities — metallic nanogaps fabricated deterministically around a chosen emitter — the group reaches a regime far beyond the reach of conventional optical cavities: Purcell factors above 10,000, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths with lifetimes of tens of picoseconds at room temperature, and second-harmonic generation enhanced more than ten-million-fold in materials with no bulk nonlinearity. In this regime, light–matter behaviour appears that was not previously thought possible, and the group’s experiments are increasingly directed at the nonlinear and ultrafast optics it opens up. Experiments combine nanofabrication, single-photon and photon-correlation spectroscopy, cryogenic magneto-optics and ultrafast pump–probe optics. The group has recently relocated from Duke University to NBI, supported by a DKK 35 million RECRUIT award from the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and is establishing a laboratory in NBI’s new building. Postdocs joining now will help build the laboratory and shape its first experiments. Recent work: https://mikkelsenphotonics.com.

  The positions span three axes of control over light–matter interaction; the balance between them will depend on the candidates:

  Spatial structure — shaping the vacuum around an emitter and concentrating the field for nonlinear optics, with examples including Purcell tensors, the nanophotonic Lamb shift, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients.

  Emitter number — cavity QED with exactly one, two or several emitters, including the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and multi-exciton emission that outruns Auger recombination.

  Temporal control — ultrafast and time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, optically dressed states in quantum materials embedded in nanogaps, and time-varying cavities.

  We seek outstanding, creative, and highly motivated experimentalists with a PhD in physics, chemistry, materials science, electrical engineering, or a closely related discipline, and a strong background in one or more of: nanophotonics or cavity QED; quantum optics and photon-correlation measurements; cryogenic spectroscopy of solid-state emitters or two-dimensional materials; ultrafast optical spectroscopy; nanofabrication. Candidates are encouraged to propose directions of their own within this scope; the programme will be shaped by the people who join.

  The successful candidates will carry out experimental research, help set up the new laboratory, including a 1.7 K cryostat with a vector magnet, a tunable femtosecond laser system and single-photon confocal spectroscopy, publish and present results, and participate in the supervision of students. The positions may also include collaboration with national and international research partners and other academic duties as required. The group fabricates its cavities in the NBI cleanroom and at DTU Nanolab, Denmark's national nanofabrication centre.

   

  Further information on the Department at https://nbi.ku.dk/english/. Informal inquiries are welcome and can be made to Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

  The positions are for three years, starting as soon as possible, with flexible start dates into 2027.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff. 

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. 

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. 

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Please include 

   	
• Cover letter describing your motivation and research interests (max 1 page) 	
• Curriculum vitae, including publication list 	
• Diplomas (Master’s and PhD degree, or documentation of expected PhD completion date) 	
• Names and contact details of two or three references   The deadline for applications is 1 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor (fixed-term) in Experimental Nanophotonics and Quantum Optics
jobs.description:
The Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for a fixed-term Assistant Professor position in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics, in the group of Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen. The position is for four years, open from as soon as possible; a later start in 2027 can be negotiated.

Professor Mikkelsen's group studies how light and matter interact when light is confined to nanometre-scale volumes. Using plasmonic nanocavities — metallic nanogaps fabricated deterministically around a chosen emitter — the group reaches a regime far beyond the reach of conventional optical cavities: Purcell factors above 10,000, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths with lifetimes of tens of picoseconds at room temperature, and second-harmonic generation enhanced more than ten-million-fold in materials with no bulk second-order nonlinearity. In this regime, light–matter behaviour appears that was not previously thought possible, and the group's experiments are increasingly directed at the nonlinear and ultrafast optics it opens up. Experiments combine nanofabrication, single-photon and photon-correlation spectroscopy, cryogenic magneto-optics and ultrafast pump–probe optics. The group has recently relocated from Duke University to NBI, supported by a DKK 35 million RECRUIT award from the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and is establishing a laboratory in NBI's new building. Recent work: https://mikkelsenphotonics.com.

The Assistant Professor will lead an independent research direction within the group’s programme on light–matter interaction in nanocavities. Directions of particular interest include:

• 
Cavity QED with few emitters — strong coupling with exactly one, two or several quantum emitters in deterministically fabricated nanogaps, the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and quantum light generation from nanocavity-coupled emitters

• 
Quantum and two-dimensional materials in nanogaps — out-of-plane excitations (interlayer excitons, dark excitons, trions) coupled to the vertical field of a nanogap at cryogenic temperatures and in vector magnetic fields; optically dressed states of 2D semiconductors and magnets driven inside a nanogap and read out by single-cavity ultrafast spectroscopy

• 
Ultrafast and nonlinear nanophotonics — time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, time-varying cavities, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients

 Candidates are expected to define their own experimental programme within this scope, and proposals that cut across these directions are welcome.

This is a leadership position for an early-career scientist ready for independence. The Assistant Professor will be the senior scientist in the group alongside Professor Mikkelsen, with day-to-day responsibility for one research direction and its students. The successful candidate will take scientific ownership of the group's new cryogenic and ultrafast facilities, including a 1.7 K cryostat with a vector magnet and a tunable femtosecond laser system, co-supervise PhD and master's students, and develop their own funding portfolio, with active support from the group and the institute. They will be supported in applying as principal investigator for Danish and European early-career grants, and the position includes a dedicated budget line for a student and consumables. The group fabricates its cavities in the NBI cleanroom and at DTU Nanolab, Denmark's national nanofabrication centre.

We seek an outstanding experimentalist, typically three to seven years after the PhD, with a strong publication record, demonstrated independence, and hands-on expertise in several of: nanophotonics, cavity QED or plasmonics; quantum optics and photon-correlation measurements; cryogenic optical and magneto-optical spectroscopy; ultrafast pump–probe spectroscopy; nanofabrication. Expertise in the exfoliation, transfer, assembly and encapsulation of van der Waals heterostructures, including gated devices, is an asset. Experience supervising students and an interest in teaching are expected. The group is simultaneously recruiting postdoctoral researchers; candidates may apply to both positions.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, funded by external research grants, and is not tenure-track. The objective is that the successful candidate concludes the appointment with an established research direction, an independent funding record, and a strong case for a permanent position at the University of Copenhagen or elsewhere.

The assistant professor’s duties will primarily include research, including obligations with regard to publication/scientific communication and research-based teaching with associated examination obligations within quantum optics and photonics. To a limited extent this may also include performance of other duties. 

Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.

General criteria apply to the appointment of Assistant Professors at the University of Copenhagen. jobs.occupation: Fully funded PhD position in Korean Studies at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies
jobs.description:
The Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies in the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a full-time three-year PhD scholarship, with an expected starting date of 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The PhD project will be part of the research project Sensing Korea: Reframing Korean Studies in the Nordic Countries, funded by the Academy of Korean Studies. Sensing Korea aims to develop sensory and narrative approaches to Korean Studies in order to explore the diversity of Korean experiences beyond essentializing representations.

  The PhD scholarship is funded through the Core University Program for Korean Studies of the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Korea and the Korean Studies Promotion Service at the Academy of Korean Studies (AKS-2026-OLU-2250001). Sensing Korea is led by Barbara Wall and hosted by Korean Studies at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, University of Copenhagen. The project runs for five years, from June 2026 to May 2031.

  The PhD candidate will be supervised by project leader Barbara Wall and will work closely with a project team comprising scholars based at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies as well as researchers from Korean Studies programs at other Nordic universities. The candidate is also expected to have an interest in communicating academic knowledge about Korea to a broader public.

  About the department
 The project is based at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, which is part of the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen. The department has approximately 800 students and 150 employees. At the department, we research and teach in language, culture, religion and society, primarily with a focus on regions outside Western Europe and the USA. The work is rooted in language-based area studies and cross-cultural perspectives that provide insight into global contexts and cultural complexity.

  Introduction to the PhD programme
 PhD studies consist of research programmes that qualify students for independent and wide-ranging research, development and teaching at international level. The main emphasis is on PhD students organising and conducting their own research project (under supervision). The programme culminates in the submission of a PhD thesis, which the student must defend in public. The programme is prescribed to 180 ECTS points, corresponding to three years of full-time study. The PhD will have to teach and carry out other tasks at the department as part of the PhD position corresponding to 840 working hours (6 months).

  A PhD opens up a range of career opportunities in academia and elsewhere. As well as writing a thesis, PhD students work in active research environments in Denmark and abroad. They contribute to the academic environment, take research training courses and convey the results of their research in teaching, at academic conferences and to the general public. 

  Qualification requirements
 Applicants must have qualifications corresponding to a master’s degree in Korean Studies or a related field in the humanities. Particularly relevant disciplinary backgrounds and research interests include Literary Studies and Sensory Studies, as well as Musicology, Media Studies, Religious Studies, Cultural Studies, History, Art History/Visual Culture, Performance Studies, and East Asian Studies. If you have completed your education in Denmark, you must have a master’s degree covered by the collective agreement for academics in the state sector.

  The ideal candidate will have a strong background in Korean Studies or a related humanities discipline, with research interests in Literary Studies and/or Sensory Studies, or in another relevant field with a clear connection to sensory and narrative approaches to Korea. Excellent proficiency in Korean and English is essential. Proficiency in a Scandinavian language and/or Literary Sinitic (Hanmun) is considered an advantage.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, you must either have a master’s degree equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (two years) or as minimum a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree (three years) and be assessed as having professional qualifications at master's level.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, we will obtain an assessment of your education from the Danish Research Agency. Applicants must possess skills in written and spoken academic English at a high level. Additional language skills and knowledge of related regions is an advantage. If deemed necessary, the department may request that applicants document their English or other language skills.

  Application
 All applications must be submitted online, in PDF or Microsoft Word format, via the link “Apply for the position” at the bottom of the page. 

  The application must include: 

  Personal statement (max. one page)
 In their personal statements, applicants are encouraged to: 

   	
• outline how the PhD project relates to other research activities at the department, particularly the Sensing Korea project.  	
• describe as clearly as possible their competencies and personal qualifications relevant to the PhD programme and the Sensing Korea project.   CV
 Applications must be accompanied by a CV (max.one page) and a list of publications, where relevant. 

  Documentation (diplomas and transcripts) 
 Applicants must upload the following:

   	
• A copy of their Master’s degree diploma or similar (if this is not available by the application deadline, applicants must document pre-approval of their Master’s thesis) 	
• A copy of their Master’s degree transcript 	
• A copy of their Bachelor’s degree diploma 	
• A copy of their Bachelor’s degree transcript.   Applicants with a degree from a university where the working language is not English or one of the Scandinavian languages must submit a translation of their Master’s diploma and/or diploma transcripts approved by the issuing university of by another local authority. These documents must be translated into English, Danish, Norwegian or Swedish. An official description of the grading scale (and a diploma supplement where relevant) must also be attached. 

  Chinese applicants must attach a China Credentials Verification (CHSI) certificate. Read more about CHSI here: https://www.chsi.com.cn/xlcx/en/index.jsp.

  Project description 
 Applications must include a preliminary project description covering the problem formulation, overall objectives, methodology, design and timetable (max. five pages/12,000 characters, incl. spaces, excl. bibliography). The project description should also give a preliminary indication of what research literature the candidate would expect to engage with. 
 
 On the website of the PhD School, you can find more information about the attachments your need to include with your application:PhD at the Faculty of Humanities – University of Copenhagen / https://phd.humanities.ku.dk/how-to-obtain-a-phd-scholarship/admission-requirements/ .

  Please do not upload or submit recommendations, publications, theses, etc. 

  Assessment criteria
 The following criteria are applied when assessing PhD applications:

   	
• The quality, originality and feasibility of the PhD project and its relevance to the Sensing Korea project 	
• Research qualifications, as reflected in the attached CV and project description  	
• Competencies and knowledge of relevant fields of academic research 	
• Level (grades obtained) of Bachelor and Master’s studies.    Please note that only one position is available and competition is intense. 

  The recruitment process 
 After the deadline for applications, the Head of Department considers advice from the Appointment Committee and then selects applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether or not they have been shortlisted. After this, the Head of Department sets up an expert Assessment Committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Individual applicants will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment of their application before the appointment is announced.

  Enrolment 
 It is a prerequisite for employment that successful applicants enrol at the PhD School of the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen. 
 For further information about the structure of the PhD programme, please refer to: Structure of the PhD programme – University of Copenhagen
 For further information about the guidelines for PhD studies at UCPH, please refer to: https://phd.ku.dk/english/

  Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC).
 The salary range starts at approximately DKK 30,200 (EUR 4.040) + an 18.07 % pension contribution. According to the agreement, the PhD student is required to carry out tasks at the relevant department to an extent corresponding to 840 working hours (6 months). These tasks are primarily expected to consist of teaching in the department’s study programmes.

  You can read more about employment as a PhD Fellow here: Employment as a PhD student – University of Copenhagen.

  International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk).

  An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in research, please visit: HR Excellence in Research – University of Copenhagen.

  For further information about the application procedure, please refer to the University of Copenhagen website: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Contact Information
 Information about the recruitment process is available from HR South at: hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2541/26-2H.

  If you have any questions about the academic content of the PhD programme, please e-mail the PhD coordinator at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, Simon Stjernholm, stjernholm@hum.ku.dk.
 If you have questions related to the Sensing Korea project, please email PI Barbara Wall, barbara.wall@hum.ku.dk
 
 The deadline for applications is 5 November 2026 at 23:59 (CET).
 Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered. However, changes may be made to the submitted application right up until the deadline.

Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Environmental Science programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Dynamic flood exposure in Denmark: where will people live when the water comes?

Research area and project description
The overarching aim of this PhD project is to understand how flood exposure in Denmark evolves over time as a result of household location decisions, and to make that dynamic available for cost–benefit analysis of climate adaptation. This is a quantitative PhD: the work combines applied econometrics on Danish register and property-transaction data, a discrete choice experiment, and agent-based simulation modelling. The project is co-financed by the Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) and Aarhus University, and the PhD student will be part of the research environments at both institutions.

The project in a nutshell: Cost–benefit analyses of flood adaptation in Denmark evaluate investments over horizons of 80–100 years, yet they treat the spatial distribution of people, buildings and assets as fixed at today's values. Over the coming decades, urban development, demographic change and the gradual repricing of flood risk by insurers, banks and public authorities will reshape who lives in flood-prone areas and what is at risk. At the same time, Danish evidence suggests that flood risk is only weakly reflected in property prices and settlement patterns – households appear to locate under incomplete information about the risk they face. This PhD project treats flood exposure as an emergent outcome of household behavior rather than a fixed physical quantity, and develops an agent-based model of household location decisions under bounded rationality that can project exposure to 2075 under alternative scenarios for institutional risk signals: business as usual, insurance repricing, tighter mortgage lending, and full information.

Qualifications and specific competences
Required qualifications:
• An M.Sc. in economics or spatial data analyses or a closely related quantitative field
• Training in econometrics and experience with R, Python or Stata
• Good written and oral EnglishIt is an advantage, but not a requirement, if you have:
• Experience with panel data, difference-in-differences, hedonic analysis or discrete choice modelling
• Experience with large administrative datasets, e.g. Danmarks Statistik registers
• Experience with or curiosity about agent-based modelling
• Reading proficiency in DanishWe do not expect any candidate to have all of these requirements. The PhD programme includes training in register data, choice experiment design and agent-based modelling, and you will be supervised closely throughout the scholarship. If you have a solid quantitative foundation and are interested in the questions, we encourage you to apply. The role of the PhD student in this project will be particularly focused on the following objectives: 1) a register-based analysis of who lives in flood-prone areas in Denmark and how residential mobility responds to flood events, using Danmarks Statistik microdata linked to building and flood hazard data; 2) a hedonic price analysis of the extent to which flood risk is capitalized in Danish property prices, including event studies around major flood events; 3) a discrete choice experiment estimating how households respond to explicit risk information and to changed signals from insurers, banks and public authorities; and 4) the integration of these results into an agent-based model that simulates exposure trajectories under alternative institutional scenarios and delivers inputs for flood cost–benefit analysis.

The PhD student will enter a research environment with a strong focus on climate adaptation. At the Department of Environmental Science, the student will join the Environmental Social Science and Geography section, which works on environmental valuation, flood damage modelling and the economics of climate adaptation. At DMI, the student will be part of the National Center for Climate Research that produce Danish flood hazard data and climate projections for decision-making at national and municipal levels in Denmark. The student will have office space at both institutions and is expected to take part in the daily research life at both.
